notes: One page, because it dates the whole life. The shape is the page's 'roughly present-day North Macedonia' plus Blagoevgrad (a reading of 'western Bulgaria'); the Greek parts have no extent on the page and are not drawn. The 'found' year (-479) is a bridge (the page gives only 'after the Greco-Persian Wars'); an earlier Paeonia of princedoms under Persia from 513 exists but is not a state with a map shape. Bylazora = Veles is not on the page. The Celtic and Lysimachian occupation dates are approximate (Brennus c. 280-279; Lysimachus 285/4); Leon's restoration is undated. The page gives the Roman after-life: 'Paeonia around the Axios formed part of the second and third districts' of Macedonia after 168. Counterparts: macedonian-empire (Philip II and Alexander; Cliopatria's -337 shape), kingdom-of-lysimachus, antigonid-dynasty, kingdom-of-dardania (this batch, if written). Gazetteer: used the Natural Earth admin-1 spellings under country 'Macedonia' (Veles, Gevgelija, Strumitsa).
